prompt: A full-bleed frame from a 35mm feature film, Chicago, 1928, a brick-vaulted basement mint lit by a coal furnace. Intimate and low: the camera sits at the height of a polished silver tray, close, tilted, the lower third of the frame filled by the tray's curved mirror surface. Holding it out with trembling hands is the mayor, a tall, skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold chain of office round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks, a pencil-thin grey moustache, sweat running down his temple, his back pressed against the furnace's riveted iron door whose seams glow orange. On the tray stands a three-tiered iced cake, one tier slumping in the heat. The crowd fills the room beyond him, out of focus, many holding old railway hand lanterns with red, blue and green glass lenses, the beams crossing through coal smoke in coloured shafts. In the tray's convex mirror the crowd and its lanterns curve into a bulging bowl of stretched faces and smeared red, blue and green light, while heat shimmer off the furnace makes the mayor's outline waver. Soot on the bricks, printing ink on the floor. No lettering anywhere.
